title: feat(jaspic): save verified Gmail OAuth credentials in encrypted vault
purpose: 通知・メール配信とその運用に関する変更／認証・アクセス制御に関する変更／画面表示や操作に関する変更
purpose_basis: 変更パスと表題による分類（意味の確定には原文を確認）
body:
## Scope
- Continues #170 and the existing vault work. Gmail consent uses the existing Google callback, PKCE S256, a purpose-bound HttpOnly cookie, and atomic one-use Supabase state.
- Requires the configured, confirmed Supabase administrator and a matching verified Google account. The sole Gmail permission is gmail.send; OpenID/email only identify the account.
- Persists only the refresh token, encrypted with AES-256-GCM and bound to the administrator UUID and Google subject. The administrative status checks successful decryption and returns only a status. Reauthorization atomically replaces the owner row. The admin can delete the local row. To invalidate the Google grant itself, revoke the app in Google Account and remove the local row.
- Uses public.jaspic_gmail_token_vault. The earlier public.jaspic_gmail_oauth_vault has a different envelope and no current main consumer. Both tables were empty during audit. No old table changes or data migration.
- Production needs JASPIC_GMAIL_TOKEN_VAULT_KEY, a dedicated 32-byte base64url Secret separate from the OAuth cookie key. Replacing the vault key requires fresh consent for existing rows.

## Verification
- 318 local tests passed and Next production build succeeded. The callback integration tests use synthetic data and mock all Google traffic.
- Supabase production RLS and ACL audit confirmed both vault tables and the state table deny anon/authenticated access and the consume RPC is executable by service_role only.
- No Gmail send endpoint, real mail, scheduled sending, rain notification code, or deployment configuration changes. #155 remains independent.
- After CI and production deployment, an administrator must complete consent in iPhone Safari and confirm saved status.
